name: AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit
author: WPAssist

sections.description:
AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit is an all-in-one WordPress optimization toolkit designed to improve website performance, strengthen security, simplify administration, and streamline website maintenance.

Unlike plugins that focus on a single area, AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit combines performance enhancements, security hardening, maintenance tools, and administrative controls into one easy-to-use plugin.

Whether you’re a website owner, freelancer, agency, or WordPress maintenance provider, AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit helps you build faster, cleaner, and more secure WordPress websites.

Performance Optimization

Improve loading speed and Core Web Vitals with tools designed to reduce unnecessary requests and render-blocking resources.

Optimize WooCommerce script loading
Optimize WordPress Heartbeat API
Disable RSS feeds
Disable self pingbacks
Remove unnecessary header bloat
Remove MediaElement
Remove Dashicons stylesheet
Disable WordPress emoji
Disable Gutenberg Scripts

Security Hardening

Reduce attack surface and improve website security with simple one-click controls.

Disable XML-RPC
Hide WordPress version information
Disable author archives
Prevent user enumeration
Hide detailed login errors
Disable application passwords
Disable comments globally
Add common security headers
Restrict public REST API access with compatibility exceptions
Prevent code execution in the public ‘Uploads’ folder
Disable directory browsing
Protect sensitive files

Design Tweaks

Polish small WordPress interface details for cleaner client and business websites.

Hide the login language selector
Enable infinite scrolling in the Media Library
Disable the block-based widget editor
Hide the frontend admin bar for non-admin users
Link the login logo to the site homepage
Replace the login page WordPress logo with a custom Media Library image
Remove the WordPress logo from the admin bar
Clean the default WordPress admin footer text

Administration Tools

Manage WordPress more efficiently with tools designed for website owners and agencies.

Role Access Management
Restrict plugin installation access
Restrict theme appearance access
Hide dashboard widgets
Hide admin notices
Last Login tracking
Last Updated tracking

Maintenance & Cleanup

Keep WordPress running smoothly with built-in maintenance controls.

Configure revision cleanup limits
Control trash cleanup timing
Configure old auto-draft cleanup
Revision cleanup tools
Trash and auto-draft cleanup controls
Database optimization tools

Perfect For

WordPress maintenance providers

Digital marketing agencies
WooCommerce stores
Membership websites
Business websites
Bloggers and publishers

Lightweight by Design

AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit focuses on practical performance, security, and maintenance improvements without adding unnecessary complexity or excessive server overhead.

sections.installation:
Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New.
Activate the plugin.
Visit Settings → AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit.
Enable the optimization, security, and maintenance features you wish to use.
Save your settings.
sections.faq:
Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit improve Core Web Vitals?

Many features are specifically designed to improve performance metrics such as LCP, INP, and overall page loading speed.

Can I enable only the features I need?

Yes. Most optimization features can be enabled or disabled independently.

Does this plugin work with Elementor?

Yes. AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit works alongside Elementor, Divi, Gutenberg, Beaver Builder, and most modern WordPress themes.

Does this plugin work with WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin includes WooCommerce-specific performance optimizations. If Restrict Public REST API is enabled, AssistKit keeps WooCommerce REST and Store API route prefixes available when WooCommerce is active so carts, checkout, blocks, mobile apps, and integrations are less likely to break.

Is AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit suitable for agencies?

Yes. Role Access Management, maintenance controls, and administration tools make it particularly useful for agencies managing multiple client websites.

Will Restrict Public REST API break forms or ecommerce?

It can if a plugin depends on public /wp-json/ requests. AssistKit shows a warning before enabling the feature and automatically allows known compatibility route prefixes when related plugins are active, including Contact Form 7, WooCommerce, Jetpack, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Formidable Forms, Fluent Forms, Ninja Forms, Site Kit, Yoast SEO, Rank Math, and All in One SEO. Site owners should still test forms, checkout, blocks, mobile apps, and integrations after enabling it.

Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit modify server configuration files?

AssistKit does not write PHP debug constants or automatic update constants to core configuration files. Selected Apache/LiteSpeed security hardening options may add or remove clearly marked rules in .htaccess only when the related setting is changed by an administrator.

Does AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit clean the database automatically?

The database tools run only when enabled by an administrator. You can run cleanup manually or enable scheduled cleanup for revisions, old auto-drafts, trashed posts, and expired transients.

3.0.13 – July 3, 2026

  • Updated stored option names from legacy short-prefix keys to AssistKit-prefixed keys for WordPress.org compliance.
  • Added automatic migration from legacy settings keys to the new AssistKit option names.
  • Renamed remaining plugin method callbacks and admin identifiers to use the AssistKit prefix.

3.0.12 – July 2, 2026

  • Addressed WordPress.org review feedback with additional prefix cleanup for classes, constants, AJAX actions, script handles, and scheduled events.
  • Removed automatic update-disabling behavior and runtime core update constants.
  • Removed runtime constants for trash retention and post revisions; database cleanup settings now control only AssistKit cleanup routines.
  • Stopped automatically writing WordPress debug constants and moved generated debug-log storage under the uploads directory.
  • Updated Plugin URI and readme wording for WordPress.org compliance.

3.0.7 – July 1, 2026

  • Improved public REST API restriction compatibility for known REST API endpoints used by forms, WooCommerce, SEO, analytics, and related integrations.
  • Cleaned up REST route detection to avoid nonce warnings during public route checks.

3.0.6 – June 30, 2026

  • Code cleanup and compliance improvements for WordPress.org submission.
  • Renamed plugin branding, package folder, main plugin file, text domain, and POT file to AssistKit – Site Optimizer Toolkit.
  • Updated Maintenance Mode to use the Design tab custom login logo first, then fall back to the active theme custom logo.
  • Confirmed Tested up to value for WordPress 7.0 compatibility.

  • Renamed plugin branding to Site Optimizer Toolkit for WordPress.org submission.
  • Removed legacy Google Fonts and SweetAlert assets.
  • Moved remaining admin CSS/JavaScript into enqueued asset files.
  • Added an AJAX option whitelist and cleaned up Plugin Check filesystem warnings.
  • Updated dashboard and panel headers with the WPAssist blue gradient style.
  • Added subtle WPAssist attribution link to the dashboard splash banner.
  • Improved dashboard hero and section header text contrast.

3.0.4 – June 24, 2026

  • Updated debug status handling for troubleshooting screens.
  • Reordered the System cards into the requested 3-column layout and made Maintenance Mode span two card slots beside Administration Email.

3.0.3 – June 23, 2026

  • Added a splash screen with section cards for System, Database, Notifications, Design, Security, Performance, and User Access.
  • Updated the System settings layout to use three columns with Maintenance Mode on its own full-width row.
  • Added Maintenance Mode background and text colour controls.
  • Updated Maintenance Mode field layout to use a vertical flex layout.

3.0.2 – June 23, 2026

  • Adjusted the System settings layout to use a 3-column grid with Maintenance Mode on a full-width row.
  • Suppressed WordPress core’s duplicate admin email change notice during WPAssist admin email updates.
  • Kept a single concise WPAssist admin email change notice for security transparency.
  • Added site title, site logo, and site icon support to the Maintenance Mode page.
  • Simplified the Maintenance Mode page container CSS.

3.0.1 – June 23, 2026

  • Renamed the Updates settings section to System.
  • Added System tools for changing the Administration Email Address and enabling Maintenance Mode.

3.0 – June 23, 2026

  • Fixed the Hide Admin Help Tab setting so it removes the contextual help tab reliably across admin screens.
  • Added a Run Now button for database optimization with visible cleanup results.
  • Added database cleanup reporting and last-run storage.
  • Added pruning of existing post revisions based on the Limit Post Revisions value.
  • Fixed a Plugin Check sanitization warning for AJAX option values.
  • Changed default post revision limit to 10 and default trash retention to 30 days for new installs.
  • Added Design option to hide the contextual admin Help tab.
  • Tightened scheduled database optimization so the cron task exits if the setting is disabled.
  • Stopped managing .htaccess marker blocks on settings page load; .htaccess files are now touched only when related settings are changed.
  • Added Database option to configure how many days old auto-drafts are kept before scheduled cleanup removes them.
  • Added Design option to clean the default WordPress admin footer text and version text.
  • Fixed the database optimization cron so disabling the setting clears the scheduled event reliably.
  • Scheduled trash cleanup now respects the configured trash retention period instead of deleting all trashed posts immediately.
  • Scheduled database optimization now schedules one hour after enabling instead of immediately.
  • The .htaccess writer now skips file writes when the managed marker content has not changed, preventing unnecessary timestamp updates.
  • Added Design option for replacing the default WordPress login page logo with a custom Media Library image.
  • Added optional Performance toggles for disabling WordPress embeds and comment reply scripts.
  • Added: Security: Hide Login Error Details.
  • Added: Security: Disable Application Passwords.
  • Redesigned the settings screen with a sidebar section menu and card-based settings layout.

2.10 – June 9, 2026

  • Fix: Update htaccess security rules only if content is changed, and only if plugin settings page is visited.

2.00 – June 3, 2026
